classification.name: ElaborateDrops
evidence: The PR changes drop-elaboration behavior from a panicking normalization to graceful error recovery. The altered helper `move_paths_for_fields` in `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/elaborate_drop.rs` is used by the registered `ElaborateDrops` MIR pass via `ElaborateDropsCtxt`, so this is pass-specific correctness knowledge. The borrowck/dropck and query-signature changes are supporting frontend/analysis changes, not separate MirPass/MirLint implementations, so they are not assigned.

analysis.summary: Bug-fix: dropck can fail only after HIR typeck because it inspects projected field types; borrowck must rerun dropck with diagnostics, and ElaborateDrops must use fallible normalization and only synthesize an error type when the body is already tainted by those errors. Otherwise a recoverable projection-normalization error becomes an ICE in drop elaboration.
analysis.originalLogic: In `rustc_borrowck` liveness/dropck, `compute_drop_data` ran `DropckOutlives` via `fully_perform`; on `Err(_)` it silently returned `DropData { dropck_result: Default::default(), region_constraint_data: None }`. Later, `ElaborateDrops` assumed field-type normalization could not fail and called the infallible `tcx.normalize_erasing_regions(self.elaborator.typing_env(), f.ty(tcx, args))`. The test suite previously encoded these failures as `known-bug` crash tests / ICE expectations, e.g. `//@ known-bug: #103899` and `//@ known-bug: #135039`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, a failed dropck normalization was transformed into empty/default drop data and compilation continued to drop elaboration, where an infallible field-type normalization was attempted. That converted a diagnosable type error that appeared only in dropck into a compiler panic/ICE. This is a correctness/error-recovery bug, not an optimization: the invariant violated is that `ElaborateDrops` may only use an error placeholder type after the body has been marked `tainted_by_errors` by the same failed dropck normalization, and all other normalization failures must remain compiler bugs.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs whose local/field types contain associated-type projections, especially nested projections, GAT projections, or projections whose normalization is ambiguous and therefore may fail only when dropck descends into fields. Concrete examples from the patch/issues include `Option<<<Backend as AuthnBackend>::User as AuthUser>::Id>`, `Cow<'a, [T]>` with ambiguity between `T: Clone` and `[T]: Clone`, and a GAT field requiring `<T1 as Trait1>::Associated: Clone`. Programs where all field types normalize successfully form the success side; the failing side differs by using such a projection whose normalization is not guaranteed by HIR typeck.
analysis.trigger: During MIR borrowck/liveness, `compute_drop_data` performs the `DropckOutlives` type-op for a local type and gets `Err`/`NoSolution`; the error is only discoverable in dropck, not HIR typeck. If borrowck swallows it, `ElaborateDrops` later calls `normalize_erasing_regions` on a field type and panics instead of emitting the expected type error.
preconditions: The program reaches MIR borrowck/dropck; dropck is not run on HIR, so HIR typeck need not have errored first.
A local or field type contains a type projection whose normalization fails only while dropck looks inside fields.
The failure may be a missing trait bound (E0277), an ambiguous implementation (E0284), or a GAT-associated bound failure.
`ElaborateDrops` runs with `typing_env().typing_mode == ty::TypingMode::PostAnalysis` and needs the field type for place construction.

The recovery in `ElaborateDrops` requires the MIR body's `tainted_by_errors` to have been set by the preceding dropck diagnostic; otherwise the normalization failure is still an internal compiler error.
pitfalls: Do not treat `Err(_)` from `DropckOutlives::fully_perform` as an empty successful drop result; that silently defers the failure to a later pass.

Do not use infallible `normalize_erasing_regions` for a normalization that can fail due to user type errors; use `try_normalize_erasing_regions` and recover only when the body is already error-tainted.

Do not rely on the `ErrorGuaranteed` returned by `fully_perform`; the patch comment says it comes from `delay_span_bug`, so borrowck must rerun dropck outside the query to produce real fulfillment diagnostics.
When rerunning dropck with diagnostics, propagate/select the actual obligations, including ambiguity and GAT errors; if the rerun produces no errors, `span_bug!` rather than silently continuing.
Changing `adt_dtorck_constraint` to be infallible requires handling unresolved `Placeholder`/`Bound`/`Infer`/`Error` types via `span_delayed_bug`, not silently returning success.
When normalizing `dtorck_types`, a failed `query_normalize` must fall back to `deeply_normalize` and then return selected errors, not discard them.
Regression tests must assert the real diagnostics such as `E0277`/`E0284` instead of merely checking for no ICE, and should cover async, ambiguity, GAT, and nested-projection cases.
analysis.testStrategy: Use compile-fail UI tests under `tests/ui/dropck/` with `//~^ ERROR ...` annotations and checked `.stderr`, plus the typeck regression. The patch adds `dropck-only-error.rs` for the missing `User: AuthUser` bound, `dropck-only-error-async.rs` for the async form, `dropck-only-error-ambiguity.rs` for ambiguous `<[T] as ToOwned>::Owned`, and `dropck-only-error-gat.rs` for the GAT `Clone` bound. It also converts crash tests to normal UI tests, e.g. `issue-103899.rs` now expects `the trait bound \`(): BaseWithAssoc\` is not satisfied [E0277]`, and removes `//@ known-bug`, `//@ failure-status: 101`, and `//@ dont-check-compiler-stderr`. Keep both `current` and `next` solver stderr revisions where the original test used them.
evidence: Borrowck generally assumes that any queries it runs for type checking will succeed, thinking that HIR typeck will have errored first if there was a problem. However as of #98641, dropck isn't run on HIR, so there's no direct guarantee that it doesn't error.

While improvements to trait solving might fix this in the future, for now we go for a pragmatic solution of emitting an error from borrowck (by rerunning dropck outside of a query) and making drop elaboration check if an error has been emitted previously before panicking for a failed normalization.
Err(_) => DropData { dropck_result: Default::default(), region_constraint_data: None },
// We don't run dropck on HIR, and dropck looks inside fields of
// types, so there's no guarantee that it succeeds. We also
// can't rely on the the `ErrorGuaranteed` from `fully_perform` here
span_bug!(span, "Rerunning drop data query produced no error.");
// The type error for normalization may have been in dropck: see
// `compute_drop_data` in rustc_borrowck, in which case we wouldn't have
// deleted the MIR body and could have an error here as well.
.expect("Error in drop elaboration not found by dropck."),
tcx.dcx().span_delayed_bug(span, format!("Unresolved type in dropck: {:?}.", ty));
// Test that we don't ICE for a typeck error that only shows up in dropck
//~^ ERROR the trait bound `User: AuthUser` is not satisfied [E0277]
//~^ ERROR the trait bound `(): BaseWithAssoc` is not satisfied [E0277]

passes.name: ElaborateDrops
evidence: The PR changes drop-elaboration behavior from a panicking normalization to graceful error recovery. The altered helper `move_paths_for_fields` in `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/elaborate_drop.rs` is used by the registered `ElaborateDrops` MIR pass via `ElaborateDropsCtxt`, so this is pass-specific correctness knowledge. The borrowck/dropck and query-signature changes are supporting frontend/analysis changes, not separate MirPass/MirLint implementations, so they are not assigned.
